title: excerpt from sisterhood
text:
We walk. Shops lighting up from inside showing souvenirs and her hair, curly in a bun. Are you in college? she asks. No—I work in a hotel now. Eyes met for a moment. More appraisal. First from her, then Vodnik himself perched on the statue next to the central market as she, hand on my arm veers me left on pavement, past the market, the water fountain where people fill their bottles staring at us. Reach for my hand. Reach for my hand. She doesn't.

On the dragon bridge I don't think of Mateo and ask what she does. She shows me a hand. What do you think? I reach with eyes instead of fingers, callouses and cuts faded white, while some still pink. Something with your hands? I ask. She laughs. A gruff noise that sinks somewhere inside me. Something like that, she says. Diverge from path and follow alongside Ljubljanica, then left on cobble and right on pavement, past groups of loud people looking back as they pass us and I look at her to see if she'll react. But she doesn't.

When pavement ends again, she reaches for my hand as we run-cross street. She lets go. My pulse doesn't. There's concrete everywhere now. Under our feet, up to the sky—two—four—eight—twelve concrete high. The cracked sculpture sphere over the running fountain revealing the smaller sphere inside. We stop so she can roll another cigarette. Want one? I shake my head as I peer inside the craked layer.

"What do you make of it?" she asks, eyes still on the diaphanous paper, filter-tip resting on the corner of her lips.

"I don't know—you tell me."

She smiles and places it on the paper. "You must think something of it. Where does your mind go when you look at it?"

"A ball. Rolling into a ball. Protected by something, while leaving a part of yourself open?"

She nods, standing on the tips of her feet, then down, rolling back and forth lights her cigarette, "Interesting."

Is she just saying that? "What about you?"

"Hm," she muses, dragging a deep smoke filled breath and staring at it, eyes squinting. She lets the smoke out, circling the fountain, stopping close to me. "Well, for one it's bronze. It's unpliable. You cast it into a mould and it stays like that, it doesn't give much and you need power tools to sculpt it."

She inhales her cigarette again, eyes still on the sculpture. Not quite what I expected and now she seems to be somewhere where I can't follow her.

"What do you work with?"

"Wood."

"Interesting," I say, trying to sound as interesting as she did.

She looks at me and smiles, eyes dancing over my face, settled on my lips. My pulse picks up again.

"Can I kiss you?" she asks.

title: excerpt from the box
text:
It wasn’t on the menu at Lucky, but I’d worked enough bars and watched enough videos to know how to make it. I stirred it slowly, watching as the amber liquid settled into the glass, rich and deep. A final twist of lemon peel, and it was done. No garnish overload, no sugar-rimmed bullshit. Just substance.

Little Mouse returned as I slid it across the bar. “What is it?”
“Vieux Carré.”
She blinked. “French?”
“New Orleans.”
“Fancy.”
“Strong,” I corrected.
She hesitated. “So... like, should I warn her?”
I smirked. “Nope. If she really knows her drinks, she’ll get it.”

Little Mouse squinted, unconvinced but took it anyway. I watched as she placed it in front of the woman, who barely looked up, just wrapped her fingers around the glass and lifted it slightly, inspecting it like a critic. Then—she took a sip. I didn’t look away. I wanted to see it. That first flicker of reaction, the barely-there nod of approval.

She set the glass down, licking a hint of citrus from her lip before looking straight at me. And then—she smiled. Not big. Just the kind that said, Interesting. You pass. I raised a brow, tipping my chin slightly, not giving her more than that. Yeah, lady. I know what I’m doing. Now leave me a big tip.

title: excerpt from companionship
text:
I looked over my shoulder and Helene was rubbing her wrist, staring at a fixed point on the light orange painted wall.

"When Toomas was away, we didn't always know where he was. Sometimes weeks passed without a letter. You learn to imagine the worst."

She rarely spoke of her late husband, but given that black-and-white photo of his hung on the wall in the living room, she must have cared about him. The kettle rang just as I started drying the pan with a rag I picked up from the stove handle and turned around to watch Helene pour the hot water into two teacups she had set on the counter.

"Did he write often?" I asked.

"He did at first. He had terrible handwriting and didn't write much, but he said once that he enjoyed the lengthy letters I wrote to him, telling him about the children, the house—we lived closer to Narva at the time and how the crops were growing—we had a lot of that in Kudruküla—and—oh, did you see on the news how a few weeks ago houses in the Kudruküla were flooded and some residents were evacuated? Such a pity."

I dried my hands on the towel and sat down at the table. The chair creaked and I picked up the tea and brought it closer; the steam felt quite pleasant on my face, almost burning my tongue on the bitter-tasting liquid.

"You wrote about crops?"

She chuckled.

"You write about whatever is in front of you. I still remember the wet smell in the air as we dug up the potatoes in the cold, frost coming early and the cabbage heads being too small one year. But it was better to have food in the cellar than nothing at all. We had to share most of the crops with the cooperative, but it was better than being in some of the other neighborhoods, closer to Narva."

title: anaphalis
text:
I searched the fields for you in vain,
a fleeting ghost in mist and rain.
a silver bloom in morning's glow,
yet silence lingers where you grow.

you stretched beneath the golden rays,
your weary stem in warmth would sway.
the earth embraced you, rich and deep,
a tender place for roots to keep.

the wind would hum, you'd bend in tune,
a voice both sharp and soft as plume.
a petal's hush, a shrill delight,
a song that lingers past the night.

you thrived in soil, in autumn's air,
in hands that time cannot repair.
your touch—so light, like woven lace,
your form—a ghost time can't erase.

but now you rest where frost won't fade,
your petals pale, your breath unmade.
yet love defies what death demands—
what once was lost, the mind still recounts.

title: orchestrion
text:
hush, hush
you mustn't talk too much
I fear you must be out of touch
your mechanism doth protest too much
spin, spin
delicate arms, thin
merry-go-round-tailspin
you never leave your black tin
clink, clink
playground out of sync
welded, dusted to the brink
bound to bypass a magic link
plink, plink
a note as black as ink
antique descant one might think
scrape-clink
clink, cli—clink
quiescence—
quietude—
dust has—
taken—
root.
